title: Three Old Questions: Who Am I, Where From, What Holds It Together
reflection: Notice, without fixing, one moment with good rhythm and one that has lost it. Once a day, step back and ask what is observing the body, the breath and a thought. You are training the eye for Ritam.

questions.q: In the spectrum of Conversation 4.1, what does the ‘zero’ end stand for?
o: Nothing at all: an empty state in which no experience is possible, such as that of a dreamless sleep.
The source, the unmanifest still point that everything arises from, and the awareness you rested in.
The weakest kind of thought, which is so faint that it can hardly be told from a state of no thought.
The first of a long series of numbers that must be counted in order, one after the other, to be reached.
questions.e: Zero here does not mean nothing but the source. At the other end, one through nine, is the most specific thing you can point to. It is a spectrum and not a fence: deep sleep is nearer zero than waking, and the pause between two breaths is nearer zero than the breath.
questions.c: Zero is the source, not nothing

questions.q: Sarah is completely lost in worry and fears that the awareness Swamiji pointed to has gone. What does he say?
o: It can go for a time, and only returns when the worry has passed and the mind has become still again.
It cannot go anywhere, for it is what the worry is happening in; she was remembering, not making calm.
It was never there to begin with, so what she felt in the practice was only a pleasant kind of relief.
It is always there, but she can reach it only in a long and quiet sitting at the start of the day.
questions.e: The most truly you, the awareness at the zero pole, is available wherever on the band your attention happens to be sitting. That is why the one-breath doorway worked: you were not manufacturing calm but remembering where you stood.
questions.c: Awareness is what the worry appears in

questions.q: What does the prism and white light show about the unmanifest and the manifest?
o: White light is plain and the rainbow is an addition, so the manifest is something laid over the source.
The rainbow is the real thing and white light is a name for the sum of its colours, once they are added.
White light and the rainbow are one reality in two views: Being, undivided, and Becoming, spread out.
White light and the rainbow are two separate realities, one standing above the other in the order of things.
questions.e: The colours were in the white light before the prism; it only reveals what was there. The unmanifest source is reality undivided, and the manifest world is the same reality spread into its colours. The Īśa Upaniṣad says it directly: from the whole, the whole arises, and the whole remains.
questions.c: Being and Becoming: one reality, two views

questions.q: “The number zero carries no value of its own, yet it makes every other position possible, and the source plays the same role in nature.”
questions.e: Try writing ten, a hundred or a thousand without it. The source is not a thing but the field of availability every thing arises from, like the physicist’s vacuum, which is not nothing but the quietest condition of an underlying field.

questions.q: Dr Watson sees patients with burnout, insomnia and rumination. Which reading of them fits Conversation 4.1?
o: Each can go outward but has lost the way back in: the return has failed, though the unfolding still works.
Each is stuck at the wrong place on the spectrum, and needs moving to a better place by an effort.
Each has too much rest and too little activity, and needs a more demanding schedule of daily duties.
Each has a different cause that cannot be set beside the others, so no common map would be of use.
questions.e: Neither unfolding nor withdrawing alone is health; health is the rhythm of the two. A system that only unfolds burns out. Suffering is rarely about which point a person is stuck at; it is almost always about whether the breathing movement between the points still works.
questions.c: Health is the rhythm of outward and inward

questions.q: What does the word Ritam mean, and what does Swamiji say about its roots?
o: Right-fittedness, from a root meaning to fit or join properly, which also gave harmony and art.
Divine command, from a root meaning to order or to rule, which also gave law and obedience.
Silent knowledge, from a root meaning to keep quiet, which also gave secret and mystery.
Cosmic fire, from a root meaning to burn, which also gave energy and the work of the sun.
questions.e: The ancient root meaning to fit scattered into many languages: Greek harmonia, Latin ars, Persian aṣ̌a and Sanskrit Ṛtam. It is not a foreign idea but one recognition preserved across languages. Swamiji maps it across physical, timing and relationship Ritam.

questions.q: “A healthy heart beats like a perfect metronome, and the less it varies from beat to beat the healthier it is.”
questions.e: A healthy heart varies beat to beat around a steady centre, and a good amount of heart-rate variability is a sign of health. That is Ritam: lawful, but alive, not rigid. Healthy attention is likewise a rhythm of focus and rest.
questions.c: Health is living variability, not rigidity

questions.q: Dr Watson is asked to carry one lens into a consultation without changing his treatment. What is it?
o: Ask where the rhythm has broken: can this person go outward but not return, or withdraw and not come out?
Ask which diagnosis in the books fits the patient best, and treat the patient strictly by that name.
Ask whether the patient is telling the truth, since a broken rhythm is often a sign of deception.
Ask how long the patient has had the trouble, since the length of time shows the cause of it.
questions.e: He reads the symptom as a broken rhythm rather than only a broken part. Anṛta, the negation of Ritam, is the structural description of what medicine calls dysregulation: the same eye that recognises health is the eye that diagnoses illness.
questions.c: Read the symptom as a broken rhythm

questions.q: Sarah is told to notice one moment of good Ritam and one that has lost it, and not fix either. Why does Swamiji ask this?
o: She is training the eye, and she usually skips straight to repairing, so noticing first will change things.
She should leave all troubles alone, since a rhythm that has been broken will right itself in time.
She should learn which of her children is at fault, so that she can speak to that child alone.
She should keep a record to show others, so that her home may be compared with other households.
questions.e: Sarah admits she usually skips straight to repairing. The practice is just to grow the eye for Ritam: the family listening at dinner against everyone talking over each other. Noticing the difference in how the two feel comes first.
questions.c: Notice the rhythm before you repair it

questions.q: Kai is asked to take sixty seconds each day and find what is observing the body, the breath and a thought. How should he treat the result?
o: As data: he is just checking whether that awareness is reliably there, and need not feel anything special.
As a test he must pass, so that if he fails on any day he should begin the whole practice again.
As a feeling to be made strong, so that he must try to keep it for the rest of each day that follows.
As a secret to keep, since talking about what he finds would spoil it for the rest of the group.
questions.e: He is the sceptic, so the practice is an experiment. Body, breath, thought, and then: what is observing all three? It is the first thing the group did, the step back into the awareness that observes.
